title: Proportion of population covered by a mobile network, by technology
graph_title: Proportion of population covered by a mobile network, by technology
national_indicator_available: Proportion of population covered by at least a 2G/3G/4G mobile network
national_indicator_description: This indicator measures the proportion of the population living within range of a mobile network, broken down by the type of technology (2G, 3G, or 4G).
computation_definitions: Proportion of population covered by a mobile network, broken down by technology, refers to the percentage of inhabitants living within range of a mobile-cellular signal, irrespective of whether or not they are mobile phone subscribers or users.
computation_calculations: Population living within range of each technology / Total population * 100
other_info: In some cases, figures are only available per provider and not in aggregate; this dashboard uses the figure for the provider with the highest coverage in each case, but this may be an underestimate of total coverage including other providers. Data is given for June in some years and December in others, depending on the source.
comments_limitations: This measure only reflects the proportion of the population living within range of each type of mobile network. It does not account for other dimensions of access, such as ownership of a mobile device or affordability of network technology.
indicator_name: Proportion of population covered by a mobile network, by technology
target_name: Significantly increase access to information and communications technology and strive to provide universal and affordable access to the Internet in least developed countries by 2020
indicator_definition: Proportion of population covered by a mobile network, broken down by technology, refers to the percentage of inhabitants living within range of a mobile-cellular signal, irrespective of whether or not they are mobile phone subscribers or users. This is calculated by dividing the number of inhabitants within range of a mobile-cellular signal by the total population and multiplying by 100.
goal_meta_link_text: United Nations Sustainable Development Goals Metadata (pdf 894kB)
source_other_info_1: This is the source for data from 2013, 2016, and 2017. Note that figures in the reports for 2013 and 2016 are only available per provider and not in aggregate; this dashboard uses the figure for the provider with the highest coverage in each case, but this may be an underestimate of total coverage including other providers. Note also that these figures are given for June of each year.
source_url_text_2: Statistics and Tariff Information in Telecom Sector as of December 2015
source_other_info_2: This is the source for data from 2009 to 2015, excluding 2013 which uses the RURA Annual Report. Note that figures are only available by provider and not in aggregate; this dashboard uses the figure for the provider with the highest coverage in each case, but this may be an underestimate of total coverage including other providers. Note also that these figures are given for December of each year.
source_organisation_3: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
source_other_info_3: This is the source for data from 2018 to 2023. The figures are originally sourced from Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA) administrative data, and subsequently summarized and published in the Statistical Yearbook.
